conclusions: All two-moment bytes predicted by the parameter count are present in the two recorded AdamW _init_group stacks. No optimizer-state classification omission is demonstrated.
The _multi_tensor_adamw update allocation is a separate temporary; it must not be relabeled as persistent optimizer state merely to meet 40 percent.

The stdout state helper sums all Tensor state without a CUDA-device filter. Its additional 768 bytes do not demonstrate missing GPU state and cannot close the 27695718.4-byte threshold gap even if all were counted.
Some backward-origin blocks are conservatively classified as temporaries rather than grads. That is a separate attribution limitation and does not justify increasing optimizer_state.
The first optimizer marker is post-step, so state allocations before that marker are expected. Allocator event indices are not elapsed time.
